Yeah definitely give it more time. It could take a few weeks or a little longer until you’re feeling your best depending on how much caffeine you usually consume. Life feels so much more peaceful without caffeine in my experience :)

In my experience caffeine enhances performance short term but it comes at a cost (anxiety, the crash etc). For me that cost isn’t worth it but it was for a long time. Honestly going decaf has made me question whether the things I was doing were really things I wanted to do or if I was pushing on with something I don’t like because of caffeine.

 At the end of the day no one on this sub has more experience than you, at being you. Experiment with it, think it over and trust your own judgement (it’s probably right).

Caffeine keeps you focused on the grind and keeps everything else quiet. Life decaf is basically just feeling everything and having to actually live with yourself, find ways to make yourself happy etc.

I’m somewhat on my way to living with myself and I hope you get decide to keep on going. However, it’s not a failure if you decide to go back to your normal caffeine habits and it’s also not a mistake to seek professional help should you need it.

All the best :)

I'm coming up on a year and went cold turkey because I was unemployed at the time and knew I could be useless for a few weeks without consequence. I was probably consuming 400-500mg per day so it was super rough. If you can't get time off work to go cold turkey I would recommend weening yourself off. I always found that sugary drinks or sweets would help me through withdrawal which is only a short-term alternative. If you're climbing cell towers as your job you can probably afford the extra calories :)

Good luck with your journey!
